dedupe_keys.name: stavanger university hospital hybrid simulation of emergency department patient flow under covid 19

description: This case study builds a simulation of patient flow through the emergency department of Stavanger University Hospital in Norway under the changed rules of the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors, Gaute Terning, Eric Christian Brun and Idriss El-Thalji of the University of Stavanger, developed a conceptual model with the department's main stakeholders and turned it into a multi-method computational model combining agent-based and other techniques, with patients and rooms as the main agents, and validated it against real occupancy data from the hospital's crowding monitoring system. The article, published in Healthcare in 2022, gives a transparent account of the model's development and introduces performance measures for practitioners; it is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Coverage is one emergency department. Caveats: the model code and hospital data are not published, and the authors list missing elements, such as doctors, nurses, beds, delays from other departments and longer treatment at high occupancy. The simulated patient flow reproduced actual occupancy behaviour, including a scenario with the observed 30 percent share of patients handled as possibly contaminated. Simulation uses: a documented structure for pandemic surge and isolation policies in emergency department flow models. Related records: the Italian emergency department agent-based model (model-comses-emergency-department-simulation-italy) and the Tuscany seismic resilience study (case_study-tuscany-emergency-department-seismic-resilience) model other departments.
